incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended, ss. 6, 9, 19, 22, 25 and 43; Companies Act 2001 (as applicable to domestic companies); International Companies (Amendment) Act 2015
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Registration and Licensing Division, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum and Articles of Association (Form 1 - Application for Reservation and Registration of International Company)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required under the International Companies Act 1987; stated capital may be in any currency and is established by the subscribers; share premium and stated capital escrow not statutorily mandated but recommended for corporate bank account opening with a licensed international bank; nil issued capital not permitted; one share must be issued and fully paid or subscribed for
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Company adopt the Memorandum and Articles as filed with SIFA and proceed with incorporation. FURTHER RESOLVED that the issued share capital be allotted to the founding subscriber for cash consideration as set out in the register of allotment. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at the address of the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa, and that the said agent be retained. FURTHER RESOLVED that the persons named by the Incorporator as initial directors be appointed, and that the officers, namely Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Company Secretary, be appointed by the directors with authority to open bank accounts and execute documents. APPROVED this day following incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engage licensed registered agent and pre-incorporation name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) via licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a SIFA-licensed registered agent, execute the engagement letter, submit the proposed company name (ending in Limited, Corporation, Incorporated, or the appropriate suffix) with Form 1 application to SIFA for reservation and compatibility check against prohibited and confusing names; pay name reservation fee and obtain the reservation certificate.
required_dossiers: Identity and background information of subscriber(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a fresh name application or appeal the decision to the Registrar under s. 10 of the International Companies Act 1987; selected alternative names may be submitted simultaneously to avoid delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute constitutive documents and subscriber statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) through the registered agent; notarization by licensed Samoan notary or overseas equivalent accepted
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, state registered office in Samoa, capital structure, share classes, director powers, and indemnity provisions; have the founding subscriber execute the Memorandum and Articles, complete the subscriber statement, and notarize where required; submit the documents to SIFA with the incorporation application Form 1A.
required_dossiers: Notarized consent to act of first director(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA returns the filing for correction, the registered agent has 14 days to file the corrected documents and resubmit with the original filing receipt; additional registry fees apply for late response beyond the correction period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of incorporation fee and issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Registry Office, Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Cause the registered agent to effect payment of the official statutory incorporation fee and the annual government license fee to SIFA, obtain the stamped receipt, and receive the Certificate of Incorporation and certified copies of the registered constitution; verify that the company number and registered date are correctly recorded.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Memorandum and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains typographical or jurisdictional defects, file a formal request for administrative rectification with SIFA within 30 days; an amended certificate will be issued upon payment of the amendment fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hold first organizational board meeting and adopt opening governance resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company board of directors, meeting recorded by company secretary; minutes retained at registered office in Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting by written resolution or physical meeting, ratify incorporation acts, approve the allotment of shares, adopt the registered office and appoint the registered agent, appoint directors and initial officers, authorize opening of bank and merchant accounts, adopt the share certificate book, seal (if any), and approve delegated authorities for SaaS subscription contracts.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or written consent
Form of appointment of company secretary/agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer disqualification is discovered, hold an extraordinary resolution to remove and replace the individual and file a change notice with SIFA within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation statutory filings and establishment of tax and trade registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA); Samoa Ministry for Revenue (MfR); Samoa Bureau of Statistics
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporated company particulars with SIFA for the annual listing, obtain the Tax Identification Number (TIN) application through MfR (exempt company status will confirm no CIT duty), register for Goods and Services Tax only if taxable supplies exceed the threshold, and apply for the International Company tax exemption certificate where required by the business bank for payment rails such as Stripe Billing and Wire Transfer.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry for Revenue queries the TIN application due to missing proof of registered office, provide the SIFA certificate of registration and registered agent confirmation letter within 21 days to cure the query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commencement of business and opening of regulated bank and payment accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial banks in Samoa (e.g., ANZ Samoa, BSL) and relevant payment processors (Stripe Billing / wire transfer relationship banks)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the certified incorporation package to the bank, provide the first board resolution authorizing account opening, beneficial ownership declaration, and corporate KYC documents; complete the bank's economic substance questionnaire clarifying that the entity's activity is offshore logistics technology SaaS, and open the operating account for global wire receipts and the local settlement account for Stripe.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and registered constitution
Business plan and source of funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires further economic substance evidence, provide board minutes confirming operational decisions from Samoa, subprocessor agreements, and a telematics SaaS client portfolio; an appeal may be made to the bank's compliance committee or a SIFA licensed bank alternative.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority, Licensing Unit; Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Occupational Safety and Health Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no industrial or physical manufacturing license required; business activity is remote logistics fleet route optimization and real-time telematics SaaS (ISIC 6201)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Excluded / No EIA required - activity involves zero physical production, no construction, no effluent discharge and no emissions-generating industrial process
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the licensed software activity; if a future physical data center or office premise exceeding EIA screening thresholds is established, Samoa EPA registration and compliance with the Planning and Urban Management Act 1992 and Water Resources Management Act 2008 would apply, including wastewater and generator emissions thresholds

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for remote SaaS operations; if a leased office or data center is opened in Samoa, the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (OSH Division) requires a workplace registration, fire safety clearance from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA), and a structural clearance confirming appropriate occupation load for the premises

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Tax Administration under the Ministry of Revenue (MOR); online portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities incorporating as International Companies in Samoa must register through the Companies Registry under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended). The entity obtains a Certificate of Incorporation and must apply for a Samoa Tax Identification Number (TIN) through the Ministry of Revenue registration process. An International Company is treated as a tax-exempt offshore entity for income tax purposes; however, VAT registration is required if the entity makes taxable supplies in Samoa or exceeds the registration threshold. Required documents include certified passport copies of directors/shareholders, registered office address, certificate of incorporation, and details of intended activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa's International Companies Act allows an IC to apply for tax exemption status for offshore income, resulting in no income tax on qualifying foreign-sourced income. An IC may elect to be treated as a domestic company under the Companies Act 2001 and Income Tax Act if it carries on business in Samoa, which would subject it to standard corporate taxation. No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election is available; entities must rely on Samoa's general anti-avoidance rules and applicable tax treaty provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2003
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 per 12-month period in taxable supplies; overseas entities making digital supplies to Samoan consumers may be required to register if they exceed the threshold under Samoa's cross-border digital services rules
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa does not currently mandate real-time e-invoicing, government fiscal clearance, or digital stamping. All VAT-registered persons must issue tax invoices with prescribed content including sequential numbering, seller TIN, buyer TIN, invoice date, description, and VAT amount; file VAT returns through the Ministry of Revenue portal; and retain records in a compliant format. No API-based pre-clearance is currently imposed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to export of goods where the goods are exported within 28 days of supply, and to internationally supplied services provided to non-residents who are outside Samoa at the time of supply. Telematics SaaS and fleet dispatch services qualify for zero-rating when supplied to non-resident recipients who are not in Samoa and do not use the services in Samoa, provided the supplier retains sufficient evidence. Services physically performed outside Samoa or directly connected with exported movable property may also qualify.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Samoa Customs Electronic Export Declaration or Customs Notice of Export
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement providing proof of offshore consideration received
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry of Revenue may assess unreported VAT, impose late payment interest at the prescribed rate (commonly 2% per month or 24% per annum), and apply penalties of up to 200% of the tax evaded for fraudulent zero-rating claims. Criminal prosecution applies for invoicing fraud or intentional misstatement, with fines not exceeding WST 50,000 for a body corporate and/or imprisonment for responsible officers. Zero-rated input tax credits may be retrospectively clawed back for up to 4 years where export substantiation is defective; the limitation period extends to 8 years in cases of fraud or wilful default.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) — Exchange Control Division, exercising powers under the Exchange Control Act 1975, the Exchange Control Regulations 1976 (as amended), and the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended). The CBS administers all resident and non-resident foreign exchange restrictions, issuance of exchange control approvals, and monetary policy oversight of licensed commercial banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa maintains a managed-float foreign exchange regime, with the Samoan Tālā (WST) trade-weighted against the currencies of major trading partners. Current-account transactions are generally convertible through authorised commercial banks, subject to documentary support and CBS reporting thresholds; capital-account transfers — including direct investment inflows, inter-company loans, and dividend repatriation to non-resident shareholders — remain subject to CBS consent unless the entity qualifies for an express offshore exemption. A Samoan International Company (IC) that both (a) holds a valid international company certificate and (b) conducts its offshore activities exclusively through a licensed international-finance facility or a licensed international bank is deemed to operate outside Samoan resident exchange-control scope. Consequently, all foreign-currency balances, profit remittances, and proceeds from non-Samoan sources may be held and transferred freely, provided no movement of WST occurs onshore. In contrast, any onshore operational WST account used for local salaries, rent, or utility payments carries convertibility hurdles: funds must trace to CBS-sourced purchase of WST, and conversion back to foreign currency for external disbursement will trigger individual advance approval, hard-currency rationing risk, or mandatory documentary evidence of underlying services. Standard non-resident shareholder dividends are therefore structured through offshore foreign-currency settlement accounts antecedent to any WST leakage.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For Samoan resident exporters of goods or services, the CBS requires export proceeds to be repatriated to a licensed Samoan commercial bank within 30 calendar days from shipment or invoicing date, and at least 50% of all export receipts must be surrendered into WST immediately upon credit, unless a formal CBS waiver is granted on a shipment-specific contract basis. However, a registered International Company engaged exclusively in offshore logistics-software and fleet-telematics services is expressly exempt from such surrender requirements, provided the SaaS receivables are charged to non-resident obligors through an offshore foreign-currency account and are not intermingled with any onshore Samoan revenue. In practice, the IC should still retain the underlying licensing agreements, invoices, and evidence of non-Samoan source to demonstrate non-residence in the event of a CBS audit; otherwise, a residual 50% surrender obligation could attach to any inadvertently remitted onshore proceeds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Offshore Foreign Currency Settlement Account / Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account / Offshore WST + USD Dual Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Non-resident Foreign Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: ANZ Bank (Samoa) Limited — legacy books transferring to BSP under acquisition agreement
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account — maintained only for existing onboarding until legal conversion

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-Low with material legal constraints. Samoa does not license standalone electronic-money institutions (EMIs), and the CBS strictly prohibits unlicensed payment service providers from holding Samoan customer tālā balances. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) may, however, be used as a purely treasury-adjacent collection rail for invoicing overseas SaaS customers if the EMI account is opened in a Western jurisdiction (e.g., UK, Singapore) under the IC’s legal name and does not route through any Samoan domestic banking node. The critical legal limitation is AML/KYC reciprocity: Samoan ICs with nominee shareholders or registered-agent-only substance tend to fail enhanced due diligence at offshore EMIs unless a physical director, full UBO disclosure, and audited financial statements are provided. Moreover, CBS foreign-exchange approval is not required for funds that never cross a WST settlement point. Recommended structure: maintain a non-Samoan EMI account solely for card-not-present recurring billing from fleets, then sweep net proceeds monthly via SWIFT to the BSP Samoa offshore USD clearing account, preserving a clean audit trail and avoiding Samoan exchange-control touchpoints.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a standard low-risk logistics SaaS International Company, Samoan tier-1 banks do not require directors to appear physically in Samoa as a blanket mandate, provided the customer-risk rating is Low and the identity of all signatories and beneficial owners can be established through remote video-conference KYC interview, witnessed signatures, and certification by a recognised professional (licensed attorney, CPA, or bank officer in the director’s home jurisdiction). BSP and SCB will accept a remote opening if (i) each director presents a current passport or national ID via encrypted video link and (ii) an apostilled or notarised Certificate of Incumbency is lodged. NBS retains a stricter branch-level requirement: at least one director or an authorised signatory must either attend an in-person interview at the Apia head office or, alternatively, present to a Samoa diplomatic mission without consular availability; therefore, in-person is effectively mandatory for NBS. In all cases, the registered agent (e.g., licensed service provider under SAMOA International Companies Act) may countersign but cannot serve as signatory unless the bank’s internal policy permits a safe-guarded nominee — BSP disallows nominee signatories for operational accounts; SCB permits them only with full beneficiary disclosure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity via nominee shares or trustee representation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised UBO declaration charting every individual with ≥10% interest; legal opinion on nominee arrangement; registered agent certificate; official certificate of incorporation and good standing from Samoa MCIL/SIFA; bank reference from home jurisdiction on nominee's br/credentialed track record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Logistics-technology export receivables originating across multiple high-risk or sanctions-adjacent jurisdictions (e.g., resellers in OFAC- or EU-sanctioned territories)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Geographic revenue breakdown; customer contracts with sanctions-compliance clauses; negative-media and sanctions screening output from a CBS-acceptable provider (e.g., Refinitiv, Dow Jones, or LexisNexis); internal sanctions policy and transaction-monitoring procedure; documented refusal of any prohibited-country onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth signals caused by disproportionate pre-money administration fees or rapid RAM-based cash sweep into IC account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Founder source-of-wealth dossier; audited financial statements or management accounts for prior 12 months; board resolutions authorising capital injections; tax clearance certificates (where applicable); historical bank statements evidencing legitimate software sales; independence of SaaS revenues in the estimated ARR band.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between low risk tier and high-volume cross-border payment rails without clear operational substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Description of active logistics-fleet dispatch platform; ISIC 6201 activity attestation; active customer list and platform log-in metadata; third-party cloud billing proof (e.g., Stripe/Cloudflare invoices); payroll and contractor agreements; physical office or registered-agent presence documentation meeting CBS substance guidance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity or shareholder loan capital from the non-resident parent or investors must enter the Samoan IC through a licensed commercial bank using a SWIFT MT103 wire routed from the remitting jurisdiction to BSP's Samoa USD beneficiary clearing account (Apia, SWIFT BIC: BOSPSWSM; correspondent bank typically ANZ Australia or Citi New York). The wire must include (i) purpose code 'CB-101 – Direct Investment in Offshore International Company' as classified by the CBS Balance of Payments Manual, (ii) a copy of the IC's International Company Certificate and board resolution authorising share issuance, and (iii) for capital-above-WST500,000, a prior CBS offshore-capital notification or exemption-listing reference. Where subscription is in non-cash assets (cloud servers, IP licenses), an emailed valuation report from an independent expert must be attached to the payment instruction. Upon receipt, the bank will credit a Capital Escrow subclass flagged as non-WST, with no automatic conversion to tālā, enabling further outbound funding of SaaS operating expenses without exchange-control friction. Any subsequent onward lending from the IC to subsidiaries should be executed using an MT103 with purpose code 'CB-201 – Intercompany Loan' and a signed loan agreement; the CBS must receive supplemental notification if the loan tenor exceeds one year or the interest rate deviates from arm's-length range.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For routine SaaS vendor invoices (hosting, telematics API, telecommunication capacity) and third-party contractor settlements, preferred clearing is SWIFT MT103 via BSP's offshore USD account, using real-time gross-settlement turnaround to New York/Auckland correspondents and business-day value dating. The payment instruction narrative must cite the underlying commercial invoice and the CBS service category 'Telecommunications and Information Services – Computer Software and License Fees'. For procurement of physical logistics-hardware (e.g., GPS units), when the counterparty requires bank-availed settlement, a Commercial Letter of Credit issued by BSP under ICC UCP600 is acceptable for shipments from Hong Kong or Singapore, with presentation documentation including maritime/airway bill, commercial invoice, and insurance certificate. Samoan ICs may also use a non-Samoan fintech clearing account (e.g., Wise Business) for disbursements under WST 50,000 per wire, provided the funds never convert into WST and are swept monthly back to the BSP offshore account. All disbursement files must be retained for seven years to substantiate arm's-length pricing for both CBS exchange-control review and any income-tax-immunity assessment under the International Companies Act.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore plain-vanilla forward foreign-exchange contracts (USD/WST, AUD/WST, NZD/WST) transacted through a licensed Samoan commercial bank with CBS approval, tenor ≤12 months
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in USD/AUD/NZD on the Samoan Tālā accepted by counterparty banks when no onshore deliverable forward market exists

Cross-currency swaps between USD and non-WST major currencies (EUR, GBP, AUD, NZD) executed by an overseas licensed counterparty or a licensed international bank branch in Samoa (may require CBS capital-account consent if WST is involved; exempt when only external non-WST currencies are swapped)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Company Annual Return (confirmation of registered office, registered agent, directors, and members) together with the Annual Government License Fee calculated on authorized share capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation; standard fee band applies to authorized capital up to USD 10,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment surcharge accruing from the incorporation anniversary; failure to file or pay for more than 12 months exposes the company to a Registrar's strike-off notice and administrative dissolution from the International Companies Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register Annual Confirmation (current UBO schedule appended to the annual return, capturing any share transfers, allotments, or redemption during the year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Samoan registered agent (register maintained at the registered office in Samoa; accessible to the SIFA Registrar and Financial Intelligence Unit on demand)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, simultaneous with the annual return — within 60 days after each incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2018 beneficial-ownership regime; monetary fines per default, with repeat non-compliance potentially triggering disqualification or administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Office and Registered Agent Annual Renewal Confirmation (standing statutory representation in Samoa)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed registered agent filing on behalf of the company; notification lodged with the Registrar of International Companies, SIFA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the incorporation anniversary; any change of agent or office must additionally be notified within 30 days of occurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Maintaining no registered office or agent in Samoa is a continuing contravention of the International Companies Act 1987 and constitutes grounds for administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None for a standard exempt International Company. An independent audit is statutorily required only for international companies licensed under the International Banking Act 2005 or the International Insurance Act 1988, or for stock-exchange listed issuers. The Logistics Fleet Telematics SaaS entity holds no regulated license, is not listed, and is fully exempt from audit and from filing audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Samoa; accounting records must be maintained with sufficient accuracy to reflect the company's true and fair financial position and to enable the preparation of financial statements on demand.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The licensed registered agent circulates an annual confirmation to directors and shareholders before each anniversary. Every change in ownership (share issue, transfer, or redemption) occurring during the year must be entered into the Beneficial Ownership Register and declared in the annual return. A beneficial owner is any individual holding, directly or indirectly, 25% or more of the issued shares, voting rights, or control rights; the register is retained at the registered office in Samoa.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required; if voluntarily engaged, USD 2,500 – USD 5,000 for a certified Samoan audit firm

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for a Samoa International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 1987 tax-exemption regime; the general Samoa corporate income tax rate is 27% for resident domestic companies, for reference only.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The effective Samoa CIT rate is 0%. The IC is permanently exempt from income tax on profits, capital gains, dividends, interest, royalties, and stamp duties in Samoa. The exemption is not a discretionary incentive; it is acquired by valid IC incorporation and maintained by paying the annual Government fee and filing the annual IC confirmation. No tax holiday application or advance pricing agreement is required for the IC itself.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No Samoan income tax return is prescribed for an exempt International Company. The only recurring compliance filing is the annual International Company confirmation and Government fee payment submitted to the Registrar of International Companies, with electronic lodgement via the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) online registry system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; no quarterly CIT instalments or provisional tax declarations apply to an exempt IC.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual confirmation must be submitted within the statutory grace period after each anniversary of incorporation, as stated on the SIFA renewal notice. Payment of the annual Government fee is due before the anniversary date; failure to file or pay within the prescribed period exposes the IC to late fees and potential strike-off. No CIT return deadline applies because no CIT is payable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Item 1 - Company name and IC registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the International Company and the unique registration number issued by the Samoa Registrar of International Companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the exact name and number stated on the Certificate of Incorporation; ensure the name matches the payment processor and bank account records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Item 2 - Registered office and licensed registered agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical address in Samoa and identity of the licensed registered agent who maintains the statutory records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The registered agent address is mandatory; a non-resident beneficial owner may not substitute a foreign address for this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Item 3 - Directors, secretary and material controllers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, nationalities, residential addresses, and status of directors, company secretary, and any person with significant control.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Nominee directors are permitted under Samoan law, but the registered agent must hold beneficial ownership information under AML/CFT rules; do not submit incomplete or false controller details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Item 4 - Share capital and shareholder register details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorised and issued share capital, class of shares, number of shares held, and identity of registered shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Samoa IC law allows non-resident ownership and has no minimum capital requirement; shares may be held by corporate nominees, but the actual beneficial owner must be disclosed to the registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Item 5 - Declaration of offshore business and no Samoan-source activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement confirming that the IC has not carried on business in Samoa with Samoan residents and has not derived Samoan-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a logistics-fleet SaaS company, state that all customer contracts, SaaS platform usage, and telematics data services are performed outside Samoa; if any Samoan-source activity occurs, the IC exemption can be lost.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual IC confirmation attracts late filing fees and accruing daily surcharges on unpaid annual Government fees. Persistent non-filing leads to administrative strike-off and dissolution of the IC. No CIT late-filing penalty applies because no CIT return is due; however, knowingly filing a false statutory declaration or false tax-exemption statement is punishable by fines and imprisonment under Samoan law.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% statutory dividend withholding tax on distributions paid by a Samoa International Company to non-resident shareholders. Dividends, capital distributions, share premium returns, and liquidation proceeds are exempt from Samoan income tax and dividend WHT under the IC tax-exemption regime.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No treaty relief filing is required in Samoa because the IC generates no Samoan withholding tax to reduce. If the shareholder's residence country requires a Samoa Tax Residency Certificate or treaty-residence evidence, the IC may apply to the Samoa Ministry of Revenue with the certificate of incorporation, annual confirmation receipt, register of directors and shareholders, and copies of offshore service contracts proving non-Samoan-source activity. The treaty relief procedure is triggered by the residence-country tax authority, not by the Samoa IC payer.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and debt interest paid by an exempt International Company in connection with fleet-route optimisation software licences or intercompany financing are subject to 0% Samoa withholding tax, provided the IP is exploited outside Samoa and the lender or licensor is not trading in Samoa. No treaty rate is invoked because the domestic IC exemption fully eliminates Samoan WHT. The non-resident recipient remains subject to taxation and transfer-pricing rules in its own residence jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Samoa has no statutory transfer-pricing documentation threshold for an exempt International Company because the IC is outside the domestic CIT net. As a defensive compliance practice, maintain contemporaneous master-file and local-file-level analysis for intercompany SaaS licensing, data-access, and logistics-dispatch service transactions when annual covered revenue exceeds WST 1,000,000 or the equivalent in foreign currency, as foreign tax authorities will expect arm's-length returns on the group functions, assets, and risks.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime for International Companies. IC tax exemption is conditioned on the absence of Samoan-source business and on the entity being an offshore vehicle with a registered office and licensed registered agent in Samoa. If an IC is managed or controlled from Samoa, carries on Samoan-resident business, or acts as a conduit without commercial substance, the exemption can be revoked or disregarded. For the logistics-fleet dispatch SaaS structure, substance should be evidenced by board minutes, written intercompany service agreements, route-data licensing contracts, segregated customer payment flows, and decision-making records showing that the IC performs real offshore activities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Exemption Abuse / Sham Offshore Company
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Invoicing SaaS licence fees and telematics fleet-dispatch revenues through the Samoa IC while the staff, servers, sales management, product development, and key decision-making are located in the market jurisdiction; or carrying on business with Samoan residents without a domestic trading licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of International Company status; retroactive assessment to Samoan corporate income tax at the 27% domestic rate on Samoan-source profits; late payment, default interest, and false-return penalties under the Tax Administration Act; and administrative strike-off of the IC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly executed false declarations or directed diverted revenue through the IC can be held jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid tax and penalties where the corporate veil is pierced. The Samoa Ministry of Revenue or a foreign court may obtain freezing orders, asset-preservation orders, travel bans, and civil restitution against the directors; criminal tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Samoa IC as a paper entity with no independent registered-agent instructions, no board resolutions, no written contracts, no operating income in its own accounts, and payment rails such as Stripe or wire transfers controlled directly by foreign parent personnel while the IC bears no operational risk or commercial function.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Samoa Registrar may strike off the IC for failure to maintain proper records, registered agent, or annual confirmation. In foreign tax jurisdictions, the IC may be disregarded as a sham, with all revenue attributed to the true economic owner under substance-over-form, CFC, and common-law sham principles.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and parent-company directors can be removed and disqualified if they allow an empty corporate structure to fraudulently divert profits. Courts may impose personal liability for restitution of diverted proceeds, civil penalties, travel restrictions, and, in cases of fraudulent cross-border invoicing, extradition and criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Samoa IC and Stripe Billing or wire-transfer settlement to collect logistics and fleet-telematics revenue without performing customer due diligence, beneficial-ownership verification, source-of-funds checks, transaction monitoring, or suspicious-transaction reporting; commingling unlawful proceeds with SaaS subscription revenue; using undisclosed nominee shareholders or bearer instruments to conceal ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Offences under Samoa's anti-money-laundering and proceeds-of-crime legislation attract confiscation of property, monetary penalties, and imprisonment. The IC's licence may be suspended or revoked, and the licensed registered agent must file a suspicious-transaction report with the Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, beneficial owners, and any designated AML compliance officer face personal criminal prosecution, fines, forfeiture of digital-asset balances, and travel bans. Civil asset-recovery procedures may extend to all Stripe, bank, and contract balances traceable to the suspicious logistics-dispatch payments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Statutory Declaration and Governance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing an annual IC confirmation containing false statements on Samoan-source business; failing to disclose beneficial ownership changes to the registered agent; issuing dividends without a solvency assessment; or continuing to claim IC tax exemption after the company has become managed from Samoa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Companies Act and supporting regulations, each false declaration or non-compliance is an offence punishable by fines, director disqualification, and court-ordered winding up. Unpaid annual fees accrue late-payment surcharges, and repeated non-compliance results in strike-off without prejudice to tax assessments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false statutory declarations commit a criminal offence and may be personally liable to compensate the company and creditors for resulting losses. Foreign insolvency practitioners and regulators may pursue the directors personally, seek mutual-assistance travel bans, and obtain orders restricting their ability to leave Samoa or the relevant enforcement jurisdiction.
